To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the presence of right-handed currents can be probed through the angular distributions of B^0 ---> \phi K^{0*} decay; (ii) the presence of strong phases can significantly enhance or diminish the effects of right-handed currents depending on their relative magnitude and the ratio between SM and NP scales.

1) the presence of strong phases in B0 --> phi K*0 decay can significantly affect the sensitivity of the angular distributions to the presence of non-standard interactions; 2) in the presence of strong NP phases the observability of the effects of right-handed currents is strongly dependent on their relative magnitude and on the ratio between the NP scale and the Standard Model one.
the presence of right-handed currents and strong phases in B^0 --> phi K^{*0} can be probed through triple products, which can be measured in a model-independent way.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the decay B0 ---> phiK*0, in the presence of New Physics.
the study of the decay $B^0 \to \phi K^{0*}$, in which we consider the possibility of the presence of right-handed currents in a general framework.
the study of the decay B^{0} --> \phi K_{S}^{0}, where K_{S} \to K^{*0} decays.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the study of triple products in B --> \phi K^* is a promising way to search for right-handed currents, but it is not a conclusive test.
the measurement of the triple product in B^0 --> phi K^{*0} is a very powerful tool to test the nature of the non-standard interaction, and to distinguish the presence of right-handed currents.
, while it is possible to probe the chirally structure of the NP, this is only possible if the strong phases are not too small.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

in the presence of non-standard interactions the angular distributions in B^0 --> phi K^{*0} are sensitive to the chirality of the currents, and that this sensitivity is strongly affected by the relative magnitude of strong phases and the ratio between SM and NP scales.

, in the presence of strong phases, it is not always possible to distinguish between left-handed and right-handed currents in B^0 --> K^{*0} \phi, and that the observability and detectability of NP depends on the relation between strong phases and ratios of SM and NP scales.

the presence of strong phases in B^0 --> K^+ K^- K^- K^+ is not a sufficient condition to probe the presence of NP, and that the measurement of triple products is a more promising way to search for NP.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the measurement of triple products can provide a clean probe of right-handed currents in B^0 --> phi K^{*0} and other B decays.
in the presence of FSI phases the observability of NP is significantly enhanced.
the study of the B^0 --> phi K^{*0} decay can be a useful probe of the chirality of new interactions.
